title: Swiggy's Instamart to Cut About 340 Corporate Roles in AI-Linked Restructuring
excerpt: The quick-commerce arm is removing overlapping corporate and support roles as generative AI takes over more work, even as it keeps spending on dark stores and frontline staff.
body:
• Swiggy's quick-commerce arm Instamart is cutting about 340 roles, concentrated in corporate and support functions, according to multiple reports on Friday.
  • People familiar with the exercise say it is meant to remove duplicated roles and speed up decision-making as generative AI takes over more reporting and coordination work.
  • Affected employees are being offered severance above statutory payouts, accelerated ESOP vesting through their last working day, and health insurance extended until May 2027.
  • The cuts land five weeks after Instamart reported a widened adjusted EBITDA loss of ₹895 crore for the September quarter, even as order value grew 16.7%.

Swiggy's quick-commerce business Instamart is laying off about 340 employees in a restructuring that the company links to wider use of generative AI, according to reports by Inc42 and Entrackr on Friday. The roles affected are largely in corporate and support functions. Moneycontrol first reported the development, and Swiggy declined to comment to both publications.

People familiar with the exercise told the publications it is aimed at eliminating duplication across teams, strengthening accountability and speeding up decision-making. They cited the growing adoption of generative AI, new ways of working and changes to Instamart's organisational structure among the factors behind the move. Swiggy will continue to invest in dark stores, supply chain and frontline employees as it expands the business, Entrackr reported.

What affected employees get

Swiggy has put in place a transition package for those losing their jobs. It covers severance payments over and above statutory payouts, accelerated vesting of employee stock options through the last working day, and health insurance and wellness subscriptions extended until May 2027. Eligible employees also receive relocation support and outplacement assistance, including three months of premium access to career and networking platforms.

Growth up, losses wider

The restructuring follows a September quarter in which Instamart grew but lost more money. Gross order value rose 16.7% sequentially to ₹9,230 crore in Q2 FY27, and the business added 1.2 million monthly transacting users, its highest quarterly addition so far. Contribution margin improved 157 basis points year on year to -1% of gross order value, but deteriorated 82 basis points sequentially, which Swiggy attributed to pricing investments, changes in customer and category mix, and the initial costs of new dark stores. The adjusted EBITDA loss widened to ₹895 crore from ₹778 crore in the June quarter.

The pressure is competitive as much as financial. Instamart trails Eternal-owned Blinkit, the segment leader, and competes with Zepto, Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now for the same urban shoppers. Swiggy's food delivery business, by contrast, is profitable on an adjusted EBITDA basis, reporting ₹341 crore in Q2 FY27, and the group held about ₹13,500 crore in cash and cash equivalents at the end of the quarter.

What to watch

The layoffs are the first major restructuring reported under Instamart chief executive Nandita Sinha, who took charge on August 3, succeeding Amitesh Jha. Swiggy is also preparing to move Instamart to an inventory-led model as part of its transition to an Indian-owned and controlled company structure. Whether the leaner corporate structure narrows the loss gap with Blinkit will show up in the December-quarter results.
nri_angle: Instamart's restructuring is the latest sign of generative AI reshaping white-collar work at Indian tech firms, a shift Indian professionals at home and abroad are watching closely.
author: Diaspora Desk
